unstated.what: Invalid date values in If-Unmodified-Since and If-Range must be ignored, returning a normal 200 full-body response (no 412, no 206); the instruction never mentions malformed date handling.
unstated.quote: lastmod = 'not a valid HTTP-date' ... assert 200 == resp.status

unstated.what: If-Unmodified-Since unsatisfied must yield status 412 both with and without a Range header; the instruction only says 'honored', never naming 412 or that the check applies also when no Range is present.

If-Range semantics: when the If-Range date does not match the file mtime the server must return the full file with 200 (even with a Range header); when it matches (future date vs old mtime) it must return 206 with Content-Range.
unstated.quote: assert 200 == resp.status ... assert 206 == resp.status; assert resp.headers['Content-Range'] == 'bytes 2-12/13'

unstated.what: An over-large tail range (bytes=-99999999999999) must be clamped to the whole file but still answered with 206 and Content-Range 'bytes 0-<size-1>/<size>'; the instruction says 'returning the whole file', which could reasonably mean 200.

Exact Content-Range header casing/format 'Content-Range: bytes <start>-<end>/<size>' asserted on 206 responses; format is given in the issue, casing 'Content-Range' is the conventional spelling (tests use resp.headers which is case-insensitive, so guessable).
Invalid If-Unmodified-Since / If-Range dates must be ignored (return 200), not treated as failed preconditions or errors
unstated.quote: lastmod = 'not a valid HTTP-date' ... assert 200 == resp.status

unstated.what: If-Range matching a past (mismatched) date must return a full 200 response rather than 412/416, per RFC 7233 If-Range semantics

reasons: The core Range fixes (Content-Range, 416, tail clamping) and basic conditional-header honoring follow directly from the issue, but the tests additionally pin down invalid-date handling (must be ignored, returning 200), the 412 status for failed If-Unmodified-Since, and exact If-Range match/mismatch semantics (200 full body vs 206 partial), none of which the instruction states.

Every hidden-test assertion maps directly to one of the four numbered issues or the explicitly requested If-Unmodified-Since/If-Range support; the exact Content-Range format is given in the instruction, and invalid-date handling is the standard RFC behavior any correct implementation of 'honor these headers' would produce.

The tests cover exactly the four range issues plus the two conditional headers named in the instruction; only RFC-standard invalid-date handling and If-Range mismatch semantics (full 200, not an error status) are not literally spelled out, and both follow the RFC 7232/7233 behavior the instruction asks for.
